summary.oneLiner: Marico delivered resilient Q3FY26 growth driven by double-digit VAHO expansion and international recovery, while strategically pausing low-margin food SKUs to pivot toward profitability ahead of a planned copra-led price cut. The acquisition of 4700BC fills a critical gourmet snacking gap, targeting a 3x ARR scale-up over three years alongside a guided 150-200 bps operating margin expansion in FY27 as input costs normalize.
summary.business: Marico Limited makes and sells branded FMCG products spanning Packaged Food, Edible Oil and Personal Care, with a portfolio that caters to consumer needs ranging from hair nourishment and styling to nutrition, immunity and healthy snacking. Its India business is built on core franchises such as Parachute coconut oil, Saffola edible oils and the Value-Added Hair Oils portfolio, sold through a distribution network of more than 10,200 distributors and stockists covering over 5.8 million retail outlets across urban and rural India, alongside Modern Trade chains and E-Commerce platforms. The Group also operates internationally through subsidiaries in Bangladesh, Vietnam, the Middle East, Egypt, South Africa, Malaysia, Sri Lanka and the USA, with the India business accounting for the large majority of consolidated revenue.

Edible Oil and Foods: Saffola cold pressed oils (single seed and dual seed variants)
Personal Care: Nihar Shanti Badam Amla (incl. Aloe Vera variant)

currentContext.strengths: Distribution reach and scale - more than 10,200 distributors and stockists covering over 5.8 million retail outlets, reaching more than 60,000 villages and almost every Indian town with population over 5,000|Category leadership in coconut oil - volume market share of Parachute Coconut Oil increased to ~57% (MAT Mar'26), underscoring the franchise's strong equity and consumer trust|Leadership in Value-Added Hair Oils - value market share expanded ~100 bps on a MAT basis to ~29% (MAT Mar'26), with the gap between value and volume share narrowing|Brand equity that supports pricing power - price increases were taken in core portfolios during a year of significant input-cost inflation while transaction-level volumes stayed positive|Saffola's long-standing equity in heart health, anchored on the 'Less Oil, But the Right Oil' ideology|Multi-country subsidiary footprint across Bangladesh, Vietnam, Middle East, Egypt, South Africa, Malaysia, Sri Lanka and the USA|Owned manufacturing and logistics backbone of 6 manufacturing facilities, 25 warehouses and 4 re-distribution centres
currentContext.strategies: Four building blocks of strategy: category leadership, premiumisation, market expansion and digital enablement, supported by execution with rigor.|Evolve into a well-diversified, multi-national FMCG company with a growing presence in Premium Personal Care, Foods, Digital-First and International businesses - a deliberate and measured transformation anchored in building scalable and profitable businesses in large categories with a long runway for growth.|Build the next decade's growth engines: digital-first, premium and globally scalable brands in multiple markets, without compromising Marico's DNA of disciplined value creation.|Stay focused on Vision 2030 aspirations, guided by a roadmap rooted in innovation, purposeful brand building and operational excellence.|Strengthen core franchises while expanding into adjacent categories and building capabilities that enhance the quality and sustainability of growth.|Accelerate the digital transformation agenda - data analytics, AI-led insights and consumer engagement platforms to reshape brand building, deepen personalisation and improve speed-to-market, enabling sharper decisions across marketing, supply chain and demand forecasting.|Invest in the innovation pipeline against changing consumer needs for better efficacy, convenience and holistic wellness.|Advance the ESG 2030 Roadmap anchored in climate action, circularity, responsible sourcing, people well-being and robust governance.|Leverage the three core assets - brands, talent and culture - as enablers of long-term value creation, with an inclusive culture of Equality, Belongingness and Openness.|Use the Marico Innovation Foundation's Scale-Up programme to support high-potential ventures across the circular economy, agri-tech and climate solutions, and run brand-led social programmes (Parachute Kalpavriksha Foundation for sustainable agriculture; Nihar Shanti Pathshala Funwala for education and livelihoods).|FY27 priorities: strengthen growth engines, deepen innovation capabilities and accelerate the sustainability agenda.|Marico's stated wealth distribution philosophy is to share its prosperity with shareholders through a formal earmarking/disbursement of profits, while retaining sufficient profits in the business for various purposes. In accordance with Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations the Company has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy setting out the parameters the Board considers before recommending or declaring a dividend - working capital and capital expenditure requirements, funds required for acquisitions, reducing debt and contingencies. Consistent with that policy, the FY26 dividend pay-out ratio was about 29% of recurring consolidated net profit after tax, a step down from the prior year that management attributes to cash being deployed towards business acquisitions in line with the strategic intent of diversifying and premiumising the portfolio. No amount is proposed to be transferred to Reserves. Governance of capital and risk sits with the Board and its Audit, Nomination & Remuneration, Stakeholders Relationship, CSR and Risk Management Committees, with an ERM 2.0 framework, a risk-based internal audit plan and an independent Internal Auditor supporting the control environment.|Climate Resilience & Energy Transition is a board-identified material issue, with mitigation through increasing adoption of renewable and cleaner energy sources and investments in energy-efficient and low-carbon technologies.|Afforestation initiatives aimed at enhancing carbon sequestration.|Climate risk assessments across sourcing geographies.|Commitment to drive emission reduction across the value chain (Scope 1, 2 and 3).|Promotion of climate-resilient and climate-smart agricultural practices among farmers and suppliers.|Establishment of traceability mechanisms enabling sourcing from origin, and diversification of the supplier base to mitigate concentration risks, with strengthened engagement with key suppliers.|Support for biodiversity conservation and regenerative agricultural practices.|Transition towards recycled and recyclable plastic packaging, with packaging reduction and dematerialisation initiatives and innovation in circular packaging design.|Compliance with Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) obligations for plastic waste collection and disposal.|BRSR assured by Bureau Veritas (India) Private Limited - reasonable assurance for BRSR Core indicators and limited assurance for BRSR Non-Core indicators.|Grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for all stakeholder groups (communities, investors, shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners), with nil complaints pending resolution at the close of FY26 across the disclosed groups.|Board diversity: women constitute 16.67% of the Board of Directors; permanent employees are 20.2% female while the permanent worker base is 100% male.
currentContext.expansion: Marico's FY26 expansion was portfolio- and route-to-market-led rather than plant-led; the routed sections disclose no rupee capex programme, no capacity addition and no commissioning timeline. Growth of footprint came through acquisitions: on May 31, 2025 the Company raised its stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals Private Limited ('Plix') by a further 8.80% on a fully diluted basis to an aggregate 60%; on October 17, 2025 it acquired the balance 46.02% of HW Wellness Solutions Private Limited ('True Elements'), making it a wholly-owned subsidiary; on January 29, 2026 it acquired 93.27% of Zea Maize Private Limited ('4700BC'), subsequently raised to 94.02%, giving entry into the large western snacking market and addressing a white space in the Foods portfolio (the brand carries an ARR of Rs 140 Crores); and on February 5, 2026 it completed the acquisition of a 60% stake in Cosmix Wellness Private Limited, a digital-first functional-nutrition brand with an ARR of ~Rs 100 Crores and high-teen EBITDA margin that holds the #1 bestseller position in plant protein across leading E-Commerce and Quick Commerce platforms. After the year end, on April 2, 2026, Marico South East Asia Corporation completed the acquisition of a 75% equity stake in Skinetiq Joint Stock Company in Vietnam, which became a step-down subsidiary. On the route-to-market side, go-to-market efforts progressed under the Sales 3.0 framework with continued coverage expansion; the distribution network now services nearly 5.8 million outlets across over 60,000 villages and virtually all towns with populations above 5,000. The next phase of Project SETU will focus on increased automation and AI-led resource optimisation, with advanced analytics and system-led decision tools supporting assortment, product mix and bill-value optimisation at scale, while expansion of direct reach across urban and rural markets remains a strategic priority alongside deeper rural penetration and accelerated scale-up of new launches and the Foods portfolio across channels. Category build-out during the year included the launch of Parachute Advansed Protein Shampoo (entry into hair cleansing), Saffola cold pressed oils, Hair & Care Almond, a no-sugar-added Saffola Muesli variant, Beardo Blackout powder, and True Elements' portfolio expansion into protein bars, overnight oats and cup oats alongside a sharpened focus on offline trade expansion; Saffola Oats and Saffola Honey continued to invest behind distribution expansion and shelf visibility across General Trade, Modern Trade and E-Commerce. Two manufacturing units, Perundurai and Jalgaon, achieved carbon neutrality during the year.
currentContext.mdna: Rural demand as a structural growth driver - improving income levels, increasing digitisation and enhanced physical distribution reach position companies with affordable innovations, appropriate pack-price architecture and tailored go-to-market strategies to capture sustained volume growth over the medium to long term.|Gradual recovery in urban consumption - value-seeking behaviour persists in essential and entry-level categories while premiumisation continues among middle and higher income households; smaller urban centres contributed meaningfully while metros shifted structurally to digital-led channels.|Quick Commerce driving channel transformation - faster fulfilment and assortment depth are shortening innovation cycles, enabling faster consumer feedback and supporting scale-up of niche, premium and occasion-led offerings.|GST rate rationalisation supporting long-term demand - pass-through of pricing and tax benefits has helped consumer value propositions and is expected to improve price transparency, enhance affordability and accelerate the shift to organised retail and digital channels.|Sustainability and evolving consumer preferences - rising preference for natural and responsibly sourced products, with packaging waste a key focus area.|D2C and digital-first disruption intensifying competition - faster innovation cycles, fragmentation in premium and niche segments and greater pressure on brand relevance and execution excellence.|Premiumisation, health and wellness orientation, younger cohorts' influence, rising participation of women in consumption decisions, demand for personalisation and blurring category boundaries are reshaping FMCG demand, innovation, pricing and go-to-market strategies.|Input cost volatility and geopolitical developments remain the key headwinds management flags for the operating environment.|India's growth outlook remains relatively resilient versus global peers, led by services and manufacturing, supported by domestic demand, policy initiatives and improving business sentiment; downside risks are geopolitical tensions, evolving trade policies and energy price volatility.|International markets: Bangladesh growth expected to recover gradually with consumption the primary driver; Vietnam expected to moderate slightly while remaining robust; MENA expected to moderate near term before improving; South Africa expected to improve gradually on structural reforms and consumption.

risks.risk: Climate variability and extreme weather affecting agri-based raw materials
risks.note: BRSR-identified material issue. Dependence on agriculture-based raw materials exposes the Company to erratic rainfall, droughts, floods and changing weather patterns, which may affect the quality and availability of inputs; extreme climatic events may also disrupt manufacturing operations and supply chain continuity. Management flags that climate-related disruptions may increase operational costs and create supply chain instability.

risks.risk: Agricultural productivity volatility and biodiversity loss in the sourcing base
risks.note: BRSR-identified material issue. Variability in crop yields due to pest outbreaks, unsustainable agricultural practices or environmental changes may disrupt supply continuity and increase procurement costs; unsustainable practices contribute to soil degradation, biodiversity loss and farmer vulnerability. Reduced agricultural productivity may lead to commodity price volatility and higher input costs, potentially affecting consumer demand through higher product prices.

risks.risk: Input cost inflation and commodity price pass-through
risks.note: Operating margin moderated during FY26 as costs escalated; the India business took pricing interventions in core categories to offset elevated input costs, and management attributes the moderation in International business profitability to escalated input costs across key markets. Sustained inflation without pass-through compresses margin, while price increases risk volume.

risks.risk: Plastic waste, EPR compliance and circularity obligations
risks.note: BRSR-identified material issue. Rising concerns over plastic pollution have led to stricter regulatory requirements and higher stakeholder expectations; compliance with Extended Producer Responsibility regulations requires investments in collection, recycling and disposal infrastructure, increasing operational expenditure.

The macroeconomic outlook turned volatile amid geopolitical developments, particularly in the Middle East, causing variability in global energy markets and the operating environment. Key downside risks to India's outlook include geopolitical tensions, evolving trade policies and energy price volatility.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity from D2C and digital-first brands
risks.note: Proliferation of direct-to-consumer and digital-first players, enabled by social commerce, data-driven insights and asset-light models, has driven faster innovation cycles, increased fragmentation in premium and niche segments, and greater pressure on brand relevance and execution excellence for established FMCG players.

risks.risk: Channel disruption from Quick Commerce and the shift away from General Trade
risks.note: Market share is shifting gradually from traditional general trade towards modern trade, E-Commerce, Quick Commerce and direct-to-consumer channels; the transition is reshaping assortment strategies, digital visibility and channel partnerships and requires greater agility in portfolio, supply chain and cost structures.

risks.risk: Emerging-market macro exposure across the international footprint
risks.note: The Group operates through subsidiaries in Bangladesh, Vietnam, UAE, Egypt, South Africa, Malaysia, Sri Lanka and the USA. Bangladesh's growth moderated with subdued domestic demand under tight monetary and fiscal conditions and inflation weighing on household purchasing power, while MENA saw elevated inflation and end-of-year energy and supply-chain volatility - exposing the international business to demand, currency and policy swings.

risks.risk: Concentration on the domestic Indian market
risks.note: Exports contribute only 4.5% of total turnover of the entity, and the BRSR reporting boundary notes that non-financial disclosures are limited to Marico's India operations; the earnings base is therefore heavily levered to Indian urban and rural consumption cycles and to two product blocks - Edible Oil and Foods (73% of turnover) and Personal Care (27%).

Turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 18.9% in FY26 from 15.5% in FY25 and 14.3% in FY24, and for permanent workers to 13.5% from 4.8% - a structural talent-retention watch item for an execution- and brand-led business.

one-line thesis: Marico delivered resilient Q3FY26 growth driven by double-digit VAHO expansion and international recovery, while strategically pausing low-margin food SKUs to pivot toward profitability ahead of a planned copra-led price cut. The acquisition of 4700BC fills a critical gourmet snacking gap, targeting a 3x ARR scale-up over three years alongside a guided 150-200 bps operating margin expansion in FY27 as input costs normalize.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Strong momentum aided by pricing; EBITDA/Margin: Resilient despite copra inflation, guided for 150-200 bps expansion; PAT: Mid-teen operating profit growth expected; Order Book: N/A (FMCG); Net Debt: Not explicitly detailed, capital allocated to 4700BC investment. One-offs: Food portfolio rationalization (mayo/peanut butter SKUs) suppressed short-term growth; Copra inventory lag delaying immediate price pass-through.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Mid-teen operating profit growth; Food business to resume 20-25% growth (organic+inorganic) within 2 quarters; Margin: Targeting 150-200 bps operating margin expansion; Order Inflow: N/A; Capex/Commissioning: Strategic investment in 4700BC to scale ARR from INR 140cr to 3x in 3 years.
order book & pipeline: N/A - FMCG steady-state demand; distribution coverage expanding via Project SETU (30% complete, 70% runway).
segment / subsidiary detail: India: VAHO double-digit growth (14% 2Y CAGR), Parachute volume stable post ml-reduction, Saffola Edible Oil soft due to pricing; Foods:Paused growth for profitability (Saffola Oats leading); International: Bangladesh robust, Vietnam/South Africa double-digit CC growth; Premium Personal Care: Exiting FY26 at INR 350cr+ ARR.
growth verticals / optionality: 4700BC acquisition (gourmet snacking) targeting INR 420cr+ ARR in 3 years; Digital-first portfolio targeting INR 1,000cr+ ARR FY26; Cold-pressed oils expansion in modern trade; Rural penetration via Project SETU.
margins & cost dynamics: VAHO mix improvement driving resilience; Copra down 25-30% from peak but price cuts delayed for single-step correction; Food portfolio rationalization removing low-margin SKUs; Targeting double-digit EBITDA for Digital portfolio by FY27.
capex / expansion: Strategic equity investment in 4700BC; Continued spend on ATL for VAHO (shifted from BTL); Supply chain AI forecasting investments to reduce pipeline days.
capital allocation: M&A focused on 'start small, scale fast' (4700BC, Plix); Synergy realization between True Elements and 4700BC; Prudent pricing hold to preserve premium vs. loose oil spread.
risks & watch-items: Copra price volatility timing; Bangladesh macroeconomic uncertainty; Delayed volume recovery in Parachute post-deflation; Integration execution of 4700BC into GT channels.
management quality / tone: Confident and disciplined; Emphasizes 'purposeful acceleration' post-stability; Prudent on pricing (one-shot correction); Bullish on rural recovery and premiumization trends.
non-obvious takeaways: Parachute took only 60% price hike despite 100%+ copra spike, creating a buffer to absorb current 30% correction without immediate price cuts; 4700BC has high institutional/airline presence (Etihad, Air India) providing low-cost sampling vs. traditional marketing; Food growth pause is intentional to fix profitability before scaling, not demand failure.

| Copra prices down 25-30% from peak; company delaying price cuts to take single step later | Marico Limited | beneficiary | High | Margin expansion of 150-200 bps guided as input costs fall while prices remain stable in near term. |
| Gourmet snacking gap in portfolio; need for high-margin impulse category | 4700BC (Unlisted) | beneficiary | Med | Access to Marico's GT distribution and cost synergies to scale ARR 3x; potential future IPO candidate. |
| Intense competition in mass hair oil; volume pressure from inflation | Competitors (Dabur/Britannia Industries - Emami) | loser | Low | Marico's VAHO mix shift and SETU distribution gains may steal share; competitors facing irrational pricing pressures. |

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.
